assumptions: Fixed-ratio equilibrium cancellation applies to the ideal-gas reaction quotient; real fugacity and reacting-interface composition may differ.
The pressure balance assumes fixed pore volume and equal H2/H2O permeance unless an additional net gas source is explicitly included.
Layered-sphere eigenstrain models assume perfect bonding, spherical geometry and linear elasticity; their numerical moduli and strains are illustrative.

costs.pressure: Pressure-rated instrumentation, matched buoyancy/flow/temperature controls and outlet gas measurement are unacquired; operating energy and gas costs are unknown.
costs.redox: Steam/H2 routing, oxygen balance, phase return, heat management, fines/strength and throughput costs must be counted; no benefit is assumed.

contract.interface: External pressure waveform or shallow Fe/FeO transformation -> pore/shell stress and connected transport, with independent gas, phase, isotope, permeability and cost ledgers required to identify a physical effect.

latest_substantive_result.summary: Integrates selected pressure-pulse, trapped-water, eigenstrain and shallow redox-strain sources while keeping each as a bounded model or hypothesis against established transport and redox incumbents.

next_decisive_step: For pressure-only causation, measure the sample-scale waveform, H2/H2O outlet balance and post-return connected permeability/structure against matched transport controls. For the distinct redox candidate, first establish an actual-material phase window and spatial phase/isotope/stress response, then compare final state and connected permeability at matched time, heat and gas cost.

limitations: Toy models use ideal gas, fixed-volume/equal-permeance or small-strain/perfect-bonding assumptions and illustrative parameters; no acquired Fe/FeO geometry, strength, permeability, creep or gas-generation rates are supplied.
The cited APT and microscopy observations do not measure high-temperature pore pressure, leakage or pressure-driven fracture; 4-5 atm is a phase-field-model output.

Pressure cycling and redox-driven morphology have established incumbents; the narrower fixed-ratio shell-opening or shallow Fe/FeO benefit is not demonstrated. The bounded review is not a priority search.
No physical mechanism, material advantage, efficiency, novelty or priority is established; scripts were not run.
publication.scope: The selected models distinguish ideal fixed-ratio pressure perturbations, equal-permeance pore bookkeeping, thin-shell stress thresholds and bonded-layer eigenstrain signs. Primary evidence documents quenched water-like clusters and pore oxide rims, but no operando pore pressure or pressure-driven shell fracture. A separate shallow Fe/FeO excursion is conditional on an actual-material phase window and spatially resolved, matched-cost evidence.
